items.title: Google Wants You To Vibe Code Audio Plugins
items.excerpt: Google Flow Music now lets producers export custom 'Spaces' - instruments and effects built from natural-language prompts - as VST3/AU plugins that run inside their DAWs, no coding required.

items.title: Super Intelligence round-up: Sonilo, Laylo, Base for Music and more
items.excerpt: Music Ally's weekly AI round-up: Sonilo launches a multimodal AI system that reads a video's pacing, emotion and storyline to generate time-aligned music, plus AI updates from Laylo and others.
items.angle: AI soundtrack generation (Sonilo); note Base for Music already covered 10/09 - lead with Sonilo

items.title: Grimes Shares First Song From AI-Inspired Album Psy Opera
items.excerpt: Grimes released 'Accelerando', the first single from Psy Opera, her first album in six years; the AI-themed trailer retells Genesis as 'God created the large language model', and the record tackles the AI debate.
items.angle: AI artists / culture (alt: Rolling Stone version)

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo Clarifies AI Stance Following 'Invasive' Tech Investor Dating Rumors: 'Absolutely No'
items.excerpt: In a Hollywood Reporter cover story, Olivia Rodrigo said she 'would never use AI in any of my music' - 'Absolutely no. Hard line on that' - after rumors tied her to an AI tech investor.

items.title: US musician given 18-month prison sentence for $8 million AI streaming fraud
items.excerpt: Michael Smith was sentenced to 18 months and ordered to forfeit $8.09M for using bot accounts to generate billions of fake streams of AI-generated songs on Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon and YouTube Music - the first federal music streaming-fraud case.
items.angle: AI music fraud ruling (same event as RS item - pick one)

items.title: The First Music Streaming Fraud Case Gets Caught Up in Trump's Dumb AI Rebrand
items.excerpt: Trump's executive order replacing 'artificial intelligence' with 'super intelligence' across federal agencies surfaced in the DOJ's handling of Michael Smith's AI-song streaming-fraud sentencing, the first case of its kind.
items.angle: AI music fraud - alt angle; dup of Mixmag event

items.title: Denmark's new digital replica law should go into effect in early 2027, says Danish culture minister
items.excerpt: Danish culture minister Zenia Stampe presented revised proposals to parliament for new rights letting performers, and people generally, block unapproved AI digital replicas of their voice or likeness, with the law expected to take effect in early 2027.

items.title: Tracing Inputs, Verifying Outputs: Validating Attribution in Music Generation
items.excerpt: How can we verify whose music contributed to an AI-generated output? The paper shows input-based attribution can give verifiable evidence of which audio sources were used in a generation and whether they shaped the output.

items.title: Towards AI-Generated Music Plagiarism Detection as a Version Identification Problem
items.excerpt: Researchers frame plagiarism by text-to-music models as a version-identification task, treating it as an ambiguous threshold rather than a binary, to detect when AI outputs copy existing songs.

items.title: Adapting a Latent Audio Diffusion Model to Historical Guqin Recordings: A Listening-Driven Case Study
items.excerpt: A small-data case study fine-tuning a pretrained latent audio diffusion model on historical guqin recordings to build an endless 'AI radio' of guqin-style music, evaluated by listening.
items.angle: research: fine-tuning music model on heritage instrument

items.title: [박태용의 뮤직인사이트]⑦ AI는 음악산업의 미래를 어떻게 바꿀 것인가?
items.excerpt: 음악산업 칼럼 시리즈 마지막 회: 실시간으로 반응하는 가상 아이돌 무대 등 AI가 공연·제작·유통 전반을 어떻게 바꿀지 전망한다.
items.angle: K-pop/Korean industry column (AI future of music industry)
